title: Foraminifera are spiral because they grow by permanent increments added outside

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Foraminifera are spiral because they grow by permanent increments added outside

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Foraminiferal shells tend towards a spiral form because they grow by successive increments added to the exterior, each of which becomes a permanent, rigid part of the structure.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XII: The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: That the shell in the Foraminifera should tend towards a spiral form need not surprise us; for we have learned that one of the fundamental conditions of the production of a concrete spiral is just precisely what we have here, namely the gradual development of a structure by means of successive increments superadded to its exterior, which then form part, successively, of a permanent and rigid structure.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XII, “The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera”; topic “Conditions for the foraminiferal spiral”. Scope: multilocular Foraminifera, contrasted with Radiolaria

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch12-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.51

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Accretion sequence and spiral geometry can be measured in existing specimens. Observational morphology alone has limited power to separate this mechanism from developmental alternatives.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct chamber-addition sequences from shell images and test whether exterior accretion with rigid retention predicts spiral trajectories better than alternative growth geometries. A consistent association between permanent external increments and spirality would support the claim, while abundant nonspiral shells under the same growth mode would weaken it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The proposed condition may be permissive rather than sufficient.

Taxonomic and developmental coverage of digitized shell interiors is uneven.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Spiral versus non-spiral architecture can be scored from existing image libraries, including the radiolarian contrast Thompson draws. The causal step is harder: many shells grow by external addition without becoming logarithmic spirals, and many spirals arise by other routes, so a frequency difference would remain compatible with several growth rules. Available images support a comparative test on well-illustrated groups, not a direct measurement of incremental accretion.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Code shell coiling and growth mode for multilocular Foraminifera and for Radiolaria, then test whether exterior accretion predicts a higher frequency of logarithmic spirals. The tendency would be supported by a large excess of spirals among accretionary foraminifera after phylogenetic correction, and weakened if milioline and other accretionary tests are commonly non-spiral at rates similar to non-accretionary skeletons.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Coiling categories in taxonomic databases are coarse and phylogenetically clustered.

Exterior accretion is how most foraminiferal tests grow, so the proposed cause is partly built into the materials being compared.
